$comment: Single source of truth for the Resizable API. Every framework package is tested against this file.
name: resizable
title: Resizable
description: Panels side by side (or stacked) with handles you drag to share the space between them. The handles work from the keyboard too.

orientation.description: Group: panels side by side, or stacked.

onLayout.description: Group: called with every panel's size (percent) after a change.
onLayout.html: a vin-resize event on .vin-resizable, with detail.sizes

defaultSize.description: Panel: its starting size, in percent of the group. Panels without one share what is left.

minSize.description: Panel: the smallest it can get, in percent. Enter on a handle collapses the panel before it to this size.

label.description: Handle: what it resizes, for screen readers.

withGrip.description: Handle: draw a small grip in the middle of the line.

examples.title: Horizontal
examples.description: A sidebar and a main area. Drag the handle, or Tab to it and use the arrow keys. In HTML, add data-vin-resizable and include vinui.js.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.description: An editor above a terminal. Up and Down move the handle; Enter folds the editor away and brings it back.

examples.title: Nested
examples.description: A group inside a panel: three areas, each with a minimum size so none disappears.

a11y: Each handle follows the WAI-ARIA window splitter pattern: role="separator" with tabindex="0", aria-valuenow (the size of the panel before it, in percent), aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-controls pointing at that panel.
A handle between side-by-side panels has aria-orientation="vertical" and moves with Left and Right; between stacked panels it is horizontal and moves with Up and Down.
Home and End move to the smallest and largest size; Enter collapses the panel before it to its minimum, and Enter again puts it back.
Each handle has a name (aria-label) that says what it resizes, and a visible focus style in every style and mode.
The grab area is wider than the 1px line, so it is easy to hit with a mouse or a finger.
